title: Major Lake Austin Sewer Line Moves Forward
summary:
*   Austin leaders approved a contract for a new sanitary sewer main along Lake Austin, extending from West 35th Street to the Taylor Slough Lift Station.
*   The project secured a 30% federal grant, and the awarded bid of $124,717 from Payne & Keller Inc. was notably below the city's $159,000 estimate, ensuring cost savings.
*   The council expedited the contract award to lock in federal wage scales for the project that were set to expire at midnight that same day.
*   Finalization of the contract is contingent upon approval from the Federal Water Pollution Control Administration.

The Director of Water and Sewer Utilities stated this project was the Dry Creek Sewer Main
on Lake Austin, on which there is a 30% Federal Grant. The Federal Government wage scale
included in the bids expires at midnight tonight; however, if the contract were awarded
today, it would include the wage scales as of this date. Bids had been taken, and the
contract is ready to be awarded. noted the City estimate on this work was $159,000, and
the low bid was $124,717.
After discussion, Councilman Janes offered the following resolution and moved its
adoption:
(RESOLUTION)
He
WHEREAS, bids were received by the City of Austin on September 13, 1967, for the
construction of 2616 feet of concrete sanitary sewer line along Lake Austin from West 35th
Street to the Taylor Slough Lift Station; and, WHEREAS, the bid of Payne & Keller,
Incorporated, in the sum of $124,717.00, was the lowest and best bid therefor and the
acceptance of such bid has been recommended by the Director of Water and Sewer Department
of the City ofAustin and by the City Manager; Now, Therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY
COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: That the bid of Payne & Keller, Incorporated, in the sum of
$124,717.00, be and the same is hereby accepted, and that R. M. Tinstman, City Manager of
the City of Austin, be and he is hereby authorized to execute a contract on behalf of the
City, with Payne & Keller, Incorporated, subject to approval by the Federal Water
Pollution Control Administration.
The motion, seconded by Councilman Janes, carried by the following vote: Ayes: Mayor Akin,
Councilmen Janes, LaRue, Long, Nichols Noes: None
